tables.name: gsd_by_sensor_and_field
tables.population: Arithmetic: GSD = framed field (long side, mm) / long-side pixels
tables.notes: Nominal; phone optics and processing typically resolve only about 50-70% of nominal pixels (contested). Skin matches well at <=0.1 mm/px, poorly at >=0.2-0.3 mm/px.

tables.name: depth_of_field_and_diffraction_full_frame
tables.units: mm (DoF); px (Airy disc at 24 MP, 5.9 um pitch)
tables.population: Arithmetic: DoF = 2*N*c*(1+m)/m^2 with m = 36 mm / field; Airy diameter = 2.44*0.55 um*N
tables.notes: c = 30 um is print sharpness; c = 12 um is about 2 px at 24 MP. Each region is reconstructed mainly from views facing it, so the full head depth need not be sharp in one frame.

tables.name: two_view_depth_precision
tables.population: Arithmetic: sigma = GSD*sigma_px/(sqrt(2)*sin(alpha/2)), GSD 0.1 mm/px, sigma_px 0.3
tables.notes: Geometric precision only; N views reduce it roughly by sqrt(N/2). Real head-scan errors (0.5-2 mm) are dominated by non-rigid motion, skin matching and regularisation.

tables.name: motion_to_pixels
tables.units: px per 1 mm of non-rigid subject motion
tables.notes: MVS photo-consistency tolerates about 1-2 px, so sub-millimetre expression drift already breaks matching.
